papers.title: Quantum Supremacy Using a Programmable Superconducting Processor
papers.abstract: The promise of quantum computers is that certain computational tasks might be executed exponentially faster on a quantum processor than on a classical processor. A fundamental challenge is to build a high-fidelity processor capable of running quantum algorithms in an exponentially large computational space. Here we report the use of a processor with programmable superconducting qubits to create quantum states on 53 qubits, corresponding to a computational state-space of dimension 2^53 (about 10^16). Measurements from repeated experiments sample the resulting probability distribution, which we verify using classical simulations. Our Sycamore processor takes about 200 seconds to sample one instance of a quantum circuit a million times—our benchmarks currently indicate that the equivalent task for a state-of-the-art classical supercomputer would take approximately 10,000 years.

papers.title: Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
papers.abstract: We introduce a quantum algorithm that produces approximate solutions for combinatorial optimization problems. The algorithm depends on a positive integer p and the quality of the approximation improves as p increases. The quantum circuit that implements the algorithm consists of p unitary gates that depend on 2p classical parameters. The expected fraction of optimal solutions is at least 0.684 for p=1. We show that the quantum circuit can be simulated on a classical computer with resources that scale polynomially with the number of qubits. We also show that the algorithm can be implemented on a quantum computer with a gate count that scales polynomially with the number of qubits.

papers.title: Quantum Error Correction with Surface Codes
papers.abstract: The surface code is a quantum error correcting code that has particularly high error thresholds and requires only local interactions in a two-dimensional array of qubits. We describe the surface code in detail, including the stabilizer measurements, the logical operators, and the error correction procedure. We show that the surface code can achieve error rates below 1% with physical error rates below the threshold of approximately 1%. We also discuss the implementation of the surface code with superconducting qubits.

papers.title: Quantum Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Fuelled by increasing computer power and algorithmic advances, machine learning techniques have become powerful tools for finding patterns in data. Quantum systems produce atypical patterns that classical systems are thought not to produce efficiently, so it is reasonable to postulate that quantum computers may outperform classical computers on machine learning tasks. The field of quantum machine learning explores how to devise and implement quantum software that could enable machine learning that is faster than that of classical computers. Recent work has produced quantum algorithms that could act as the building blocks of machine learning programs.

papers.title: Quantum Computing in the NISQ Era and Beyond
papers.abstract: Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) technology will be available in the near future. NISQ devices will have 50-100 qubits, gate errors of order 10^-3, and will not be fault-tolerant. We discuss the potential applications of NISQ devices, including quantum simulation, optimization, and machine learning. We also discuss the challenges of NISQ computing, including the need for error mitigation techniques and the development of quantum algorithms that are robust to noise.

papers.title: Quantum Supremacy Using a Programmable Superconducting Processor
papers.abstract: The promise of quantum computers is that certain computational tasks might be executed exponentially faster on a quantum processor than on a classical processor. A fundamental challenge is to build a high-fidelity processor capable of running quantum algorithms in an exponentially large computational space.

papers.title: Quantum Error Correction of a Qubit Entangled with an Unknown State
papers.abstract: Quantum error correction is essential for quantum communication and computation. We demonstrate the quantum error correction of a qubit entangled with an unknown state using a three-qubit code. This is the first experimental demonstration of quantum error correction.

papers.title: Quantum Algorithm for Linear Systems of Equations
papers.abstract: Solving linear systems of equations is a common problem in science and engineering. We present a quantum algorithm that solves an N x N system of linear equations in time O(log N), exponentially faster than the best known classical algorithms. The algorithm, known as the HHL algorithm, uses quantum phase estimation and Hamiltonian simulation.

papers.title: Quantum Walks and Search Algorithms
papers.abstract: Quantum walks are the quantum analog of classical random walks. They have been shown to be universal for quantum computation and can be used to construct quantum search algorithms. We review the theory of quantum walks and their applications to quantum computing.

papers.title: Quantum Simulation of Many-Body Systems
papers.abstract: Quantum simulation is one of the most promising applications of quantum computers. We review the theory and practice of quantum simulation of many-body systems, including fermionic and bosonic systems. We discuss digital and analog quantum simulation approaches and their applications to condensed matter physics, high-energy physics, and quantum chemistry.

papers.title: Quantum Key Distribution with High Loss: Toward Global Secure Communication
papers.institution: University of Toronto / University of Bristol
papers.abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) allows two parties to share a secret key with security guaranteed by the laws of quantum mechanics. We propose a protocol that can tolerate high loss rates, making global secure communication possible. The protocol uses decoy states and measurement-device-independent techniques.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Trapped Ions
papers.abstract: We propose a scheme for quantum computing with trapped ions. The scheme uses laser-cooled ions in a linear trap, with the internal states of the ions serving as qubits and the collective motional states serving as a bus for quantum gates. We show that universal quantum computation can be achieved with this scheme.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Superconducting Qubits
papers.abstract: Superconducting qubits are among the most promising platforms for quantum computing. We review the progress in superconducting quantum computing, including the development of transmon qubits, quantum gates, and quantum error correction. We also discuss the challenges and future directions of the field.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Topological Qubits
papers.abstract: Topological quantum computing is a paradigm for quantum computing that uses topological states of matter to encode and manipulate quantum information. The topological protection makes the qubits inherently robust against local perturbations. We review the theory of topological quantum computing, including the toric code, the Kitaev model, and the Majorana fermion approach.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Photons
papers.abstract: We propose a scheme for efficient quantum computing with optically controlled linear optics. The scheme uses single photons, linear optical elements, and photodetectors to implement quantum gates. We show that universal quantum computation can be achieved with this scheme, despite the fact that photons do not interact directly with each other.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Neutral Atoms
papers.abstract: Neutral atoms are a promising platform for quantum computing. We review the progress in quantum computing with neutral atoms, including the development of optical tweezers, Rydberg gates, and quantum error correction. We also discuss the challenges and future directions of the field.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Dots
papers.abstract: We propose a scheme for quantum computing with quantum dots. The scheme uses the spin of electrons confined in quantum dots as qubits, with exchange interactions providing the two-qubit gates. We show that universal quantum computation can be achieved with this scheme.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with NV Centers
papers.abstract: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are a promising platform for quantum computing. We review the progress in quantum computing with NV centers, including the development of quantum gates, quantum error correction, and quantum networks. We also discuss the challenges and future directions of the field.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Adiabatic Evolution
papers.abstract: We propose a quantum algorithm based on adiabatic evolution for solving combinatorial optimization problems. The algorithm starts with a simple Hamiltonian whose ground state is known, and slowly evolves the system to a final Hamiltonian whose ground state encodes the solution to the optimization problem. We show that the algorithm can solve NP-complete problems in polynomial time if the spectral gap is sufficiently large.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Annealers
papers.abstract: We describe a quantum annealer based on superconducting flux qubits. The device implements the adiabatic quantum computing paradigm and can be used to solve optimization problems. We demonstrate the device on a 128-qubit chip and show that it can solve problems that are intractable for classical computers.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Variational Quantum Eigensolver
papers.abstract: We demonstrate the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) on a photonic quantum chip. VQE is a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm that uses a quantum computer to prepare trial states and a classical computer to optimize the parameters. We apply VQE to the problem of finding the ground state energy of the helium hydride ion.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Phase Estimation
papers.abstract: We present a quantum algorithm for estimating the phase of an eigenvalue of a unitary operator. The algorithm, known as quantum phase estimation, is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, including Shor's factoring algorithm and the quantum algorithm for linear systems of equations.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Shor's Algorithm
papers.journal: Proceedings of the 35th Annual Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science
papers.abstract: We present a quantum algorithm for factoring integers in polynomial time. The algorithm, known as Shor's algorithm, uses quantum Fourier transform and modular exponentiation to find the period of a function, which can then be used to factor integers. The algorithm runs in O((log N)^3) time, exponentially faster than the best known classical algorithms.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Grover's Algorithm
papers.journal: Proceedings of the 28th Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing
papers.abstract: We present a quantum algorithm for searching an unsorted database of N items in O(sqrt(N)) time, quadratically faster than the best possible classical algorithm. The algorithm, known as Grover's algorithm, uses amplitude amplification to increase the probability of finding the marked item.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Teleportation
papers.institution: IBM Research / Université de Montréal / Oxford / Caltech
papers.abstract: We present a scheme for teleporting an unknown quantum state from one location to another using classical communication and shared entanglement. The scheme, known as quantum teleportation, does not require the state to be known in advance and does not violate the no-cloning theorem.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Entanglement
papers.abstract: We review the theory of quantum entanglement, including its characterization, quantification, and applications. We discuss entanglement as a resource for quantum information processing, including quantum teleportation, superdense coding, and quantum key distribution.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Error Mitigation
papers.abstract: We present a method for mitigating errors in quantum computations without the overhead of full quantum error correction. The method, known as zero-noise extrapolation, works by deliberately amplifying the noise and then extrapolating back to the zero-noise limit. We demonstrate the method on a superconducting quantum processor.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Networks
papers.abstract: We review the progress in quantum networks, including quantum repeaters, quantum key distribution, and distributed quantum computing. We discuss the challenges of building a quantum internet and the potential applications of quantum networks.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Chemistry
papers.institution: University of Oxford / University of Tokyo / University of Toronto / UCL
papers.abstract: We review the application of quantum computing to quantum chemistry, including the simulation of molecular systems, the calculation of molecular properties, and the design of new materials. We discuss the algorithms, hardware, and software required for quantum chemistry on quantum computers.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Optimization
papers.abstract: We review the application of quantum computing to optimization problems, including the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA), quantum annealing, and variational quantum algorithms. We discuss the potential advantages of quantum optimization and the challenges of implementing it on near-term quantum devices.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Simulation
papers.abstract: We show that quantum computers can efficiently simulate quantum systems that are intractable for classical computers. The simulation uses the Trotter-Suzuki decomposition to approximate the time evolution of the quantum system. We discuss the application of quantum simulation to condensed matter physics, high-energy physics, and quantum chemistry.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Fourier Transform
papers.abstract: We describe an efficient quantum algorithm for computing the discrete Fourier transform. The quantum Fourier transform (QFT) is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, including Shor's factoring algorithm and quantum phase estimation. The QFT can be implemented with O(n^2) quantum gates, exponentially faster than the classical fast Fourier transform.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Walks
papers.institution: University of Waterloo / UC Berkeley / Tel Aviv University
papers.journal: Proceedings of the 33rd Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing
papers.abstract: We present a quantum algorithm based on quantum walks for solving the element distinctness problem. The algorithm runs in O(N^(2/3)) time, quadratically faster than the best known classical algorithm. We also show that quantum walks can be used to construct quantum search algorithms.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Error Correction Codes
papers.abstract: We present a method for constructing quantum error correcting codes from classical error correcting codes. The method, known as the CSS construction, allows the construction of quantum codes that can correct arbitrary errors on a single qubit. We also discuss the threshold theorem, which states that arbitrarily long quantum computations can be performed reliably if the error rate is below a certain threshold.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Repeaters
papers.abstract: We propose a scheme for quantum repeaters that can extend the range of quantum communication. The scheme uses entanglement swapping and entanglement purification to create high-fidelity entangled pairs over long distances. We show that the scheme can achieve communication rates that are polynomial in the distance.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Key Distribution
papers.journal: Proceedings of IEEE International Conference on Computers, Systems and Signal Processing
papers.abstract: We present a protocol for quantum key distribution (QKD) that allows two parties to share a secret key with security guaranteed by the laws of quantum mechanics. The protocol, known as BB84, uses the polarization of single photons to encode the key. We show that the protocol is secure against any eavesdropping attack allowed by quantum mechanics.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Random Access Codes
papers.institution: UC Berkeley / University of Waterloo / Tel Aviv University
papers.journal: Proceedings of the 31st Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing
papers.abstract: We study quantum random access codes, which allow the encoding of n bits into m qubits such that any one of the n bits can be recovered with high probability. We show that quantum random access codes can outperform classical random access codes, demonstrating a quantum advantage in communication complexity.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum State Tomography
papers.abstract: We present a method for reconstructing the density matrix of a quantum state from measurements. The method, known as quantum state tomography, uses the maximum likelihood estimation to find the most likely density matrix consistent with the measurement data. We discuss the application of quantum state tomography to quantum computing and quantum information.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Process Tomography
papers.abstract: We present a method for characterizing quantum processes using quantum process tomography. The method reconstructs the completely positive map that describes the quantum process from measurements on input-output pairs. We discuss the application of quantum process tomography to quantum computing and quantum error correction.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Benchmarking
papers.abstract: We present a method for benchmarking quantum gates using randomized benchmarking. The method estimates the average error rate of a set of quantum gates by measuring the decay of fidelity under random sequences of gates. We demonstrate the method on a trapped-ion quantum computer.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Control
papers.institution: TU Munich / University of Kassel / INRIA
papers.abstract: We review the theory and practice of quantum control, including the design of optimal control pulses for quantum gates, the suppression of decoherence, and the implementation of quantum error correction. We discuss the application of quantum control to quantum computing, quantum simulation, and quantum sensing.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Metrology
papers.abstract: We review the application of quantum mechanics to metrology, including the use of squeezed states, entangled states, and quantum non-demolition measurements to achieve precision beyond the classical limit. We discuss the application of quantum metrology to gravitational wave detection, atomic clocks, and quantum imaging.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Imaging
papers.journal: Journal of Optics B: Quantum and Semiclassical Optics
papers.abstract: We review the theory of quantum imaging, including the use of entangled photons to achieve sub-shot-noise imaging, ghost imaging, and quantum lithography. We discuss the application of quantum imaging to biological imaging, remote sensing, and optical computing.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Sensing
papers.abstract: We review the theory and practice of quantum sensing, including the use of NV centers, trapped ions, and superconducting qubits for precision measurements. We discuss the application of quantum sensing to magnetometry, thermometry, and gravitational wave detection.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Communication
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive theory of quantum communication, including quantum channels, quantum capacity, and quantum error correction. We discuss the application of quantum communication to quantum key distribution, quantum teleportation, and distributed quantum computing.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Information Theory
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive theory of quantum information, including quantum bits, quantum gates, quantum algorithms, and quantum error correction. We discuss the application of quantum information to quantum computing, quantum communication, and quantum cryptography.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Complexity Theory
papers.institution: University of Waterloo / University of Calgary
papers.journal: Encyclopedia of Complexity and Systems Science
papers.abstract: We review the theory of quantum complexity, including the classes BQP, QMA, and their relationships to classical complexity classes. We discuss the application of quantum complexity theory to quantum computing, quantum cryptography, and quantum simulation.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Cryptography
papers.abstract: We review the theory and practice of quantum cryptography, including quantum key distribution, quantum coin tossing, and quantum bit commitment. We discuss the security proofs of quantum cryptographic protocols and the practical challenges of implementing them.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Game Theory
papers.abstract: We present a quantum version of the Prisoner's Dilemma using entangled quantum states. We show that the quantum version has a Nash equilibrium that is Pareto optimal, unlike the classical version. We discuss the application of quantum game theory to quantum computing and quantum communication.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Quantum Biology
papers.institution: USC / Imperial College / University of Chicago
papers.abstract: We review the application of quantum mechanics to biology, including photosynthesis, magnetoreception, and enzyme catalysis. We discuss the role of quantum coherence and entanglement in biological systems and the potential for quantum computing to simulate biological processes.
